headline: Multi-feature models predict exon skipping; cerebellar regulatory networks conserved
label: Alternative Splicing And Gene Regulation
summary: Single-cell and cross-species profiling now links splicing outcomes and regulatory networks to hematopoietic and neural development.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inferring regulatory programs by integrating multiple features or species rather than relying on single readouts. In hematopoiesis, FAScore integrates 19 features across transcriptomes from six vertebrates to predict functional exon-skipping events. The cerebellum study pairs cross-species single-nucleus RNA and ATAC profiling of six mammals to identify conserved regulatory networks and sequence-based models. MoDIFI applies a Bayesian framework to RNA-seq, ATAC-seq and Hi-C to prioritize neuronal cell lines and regulatory regions for neurodevelopmental variants, while the basal ganglia resource integrates single-cell multi-omics across four species. The new element is functional prediction of splicing outcomes from multi-feature integration, alongside cross-species mapping of conserved cerebellar networks. The IDR analysis and lncRNA causal inference contribute complementary, less directly related perspectives.
